Updated read incorporating Beige Book insights

- Policy: The FOMC held 5.25–5.50% and kept QT, noting risks are in “better balance.” That’s a mild dovish tilt but still data‑dependent.
- SLOOS: Credit remains a headwind across business, CRE, mortgage, and consumer categories; demand is subdued and underwriting tight.
- Beige Book cross‑check: District anecdotes point to only slight-to-modest growth rather than “solid.” Reports note softer nonmanufacturing in parts of the Northeast (e.g., New York/Philadelphia), continued manufacturing softness (e.g., Cleveland), persistent CRE stress (office valuations/refi risk), and moderating wage pressures (early‑July reports). Consumer spending was mixed/soft in several Districts, with credit conditions still conservative.
- Implication: Beige Book corroborates cooling labor/wage momentum and weak credit demand, tempering the FOMC’s growth tone. Disinflation progress is supported, but activity risks skew a bit to the downside. Net stance remains patient, with no urgency to hike; cuts await more confidence on inflation.

Bottom line: Shift the assessment slightly more cautious than the prior SLOOS‑only read.
